messages.subject: limiting histogram x-axis
parts:
I'm attempting to plot several plots with the same x-axis limits, one
of which is a histogram. However, if I set the histogram's limits to
range(observations) it excludes the first and last bin:

a=data.frame(obs=rnorm(10))
p=ggplot(
data = a
,aes(
x = obs
)
)+geom_histogram(
)
p
p+scale_x_continuous(
limits = range(a$obs)
)

One fix is to explicitly set a binwidth then modify the limits accordingly:

my_binwidth = 1
p=ggplot(
data = a
,aes(
x = obs
)
)+geom_histogram(
bindwidth=my_binwidth
)

p+scale_x_continuous(
limits = c(min(a$obs)-binwidth,max(a$obs)+binwidth)
)

But this seems rather inelegant. Any suggestions?


--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology
Dalhousie University

messages.subject: extra empty panel example in ggplot2 0.8.3
parts:
Hadley,

Okay - I finally got the 0.8.3 version of ggplot2 and plyr 0.1.6 development version to work for my ggplot2 example.

By any chance can you provide an example or advice that allows an "extra empty panel" to be added to the example below or something similar?

Thank you again for all your help.

Example:

In order to keep the scales on plots for multiple data sets it appears that I need to add an empty bin in the bar plot.

I tried to do this in the example below by expanding the range, i.e. range(c(Data, max_range)) where max_range is the desired max x-scale, however apparently this had no effect. I hoped it would have added an "empty" bin from 80-100.

Thanks for your help.

VADeaths_flat_df = stack(as.data.frame(VADeaths))
names(VADeaths_flat_df) = c('Data','Person')

max_range<-100
counts <- ddply(VADeaths_flat_df, .(cut(Data, breaks=fullseq(range(c(Data, max_range)), 20)), Person), nrow)
names(counts) <- c("bin", "person", "n")

print(qplot(person, n, data = counts, fill = person, geom="bar", stat="identity", width = 0.9) + facet_grid(. ~ bin) + opts(axis.text.x = NULL) + opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(colour = "red")) + opts(strip.text.x = theme_text(colour = "green", size=14)))

Hadley, (in the below I am using ggplot2_0.8.3.tar.gz & plyr_0.1.6.tar.gz)

I may have spoke too soon. I tried out my second example, and there appears to be an issue with the "facet_wrap" when there is a string invovled in the facet (hopefully I am using the proper terminology).

Below is the example, but here is the error received:
"Error in `[.data.frame`(plot$data, , setdiff(cond, names(df)), drop = FALSE) : undefined columns selected"

Note, the example worked fine with "facet_grid", but switching over to "facet_wrap" seemed to cause an issue.

Any help is greatly appreciated.

Jason

# Note the ability to switch out the facet_grid and facet_wrap below:

Me_df<-data.frame(Data = c(1:15), Person = "Me")
You_df<-data.frame(Data = c(10:20), Person = "You")
Them_df<-data.frame(Data = c(15:25), Person = "Them")

Group_df_tmp<-rbind(Me_df,You_df)
Group_df<-rbind(Group_df_tmp,Them_df)

Group_df$Person <- factor(Group_df$Person, levels = c("Them", "You", "Me"))
#max_range<-100
#counts <- ddply(VADeaths_flat_df, .(cut(Data, breaks=fullseq(range(c(Data, max_range)), 20)), Person), nrow)

max_range<-30
#counts <- ddply(Group_df, .(cut(Data, breaks=fullseq(range(Data), 5)), Person), nrow)
counts <- ddply(Group_df, .(cut(Data, breaks=fullseq(range(c(Data, max_range)), 5)), Person), nrow)
names(counts) <- c("Bin", "Person", "Frequency")
qplot(Person, Frequency, data = counts, fill = Person, geom="bar", stat="identity", width = 0.9, xlab="Person") +
facet_wrap(~ bin, drop = FALSE, nrow = 1) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("royalblue2", "tomato3", "palegreen2")) + opts(legend.position=c(0.8,0.70)) # + xlim("You", "Me", "Them")

messages.subject: Re: Issue with extra empty panel example in ggplot2 0.8.3 when string  involved...Solved
parts:
On Windows (have not had a chance to try out on Mac OS:

It appears to be the capitable "B" in Bin vs. the lower case "b" in bin.

Works:

qplot(Person, Frequency, data = counts, fill = Person,
geom="bar", stat="identity") + facet_wrap(~ Bin, drop = FALSE)
Does not work:
qplot(Person, Frequency, data = counts, fill = Person,

geom="bar", stat="identity") + facet_wrap(~ bin, drop = FALSE)


Thanks again!
